analysis.title: GS TMT SPEC SALES: Oracle derisks raises; NOW 17% raises software debate; Hyperscalers mixed; Optical M&A in Europe = Nokia
key_insights: Oracle (+10%, bonds also better) reaffirmed its FY27 guide at its capital markets day and put a hard $20B cap on additional equity/debt raises through FY30. It guides to free-cash-flow positive in H2 FY28 and $30B+ FCF in FY29, with growth self-funded afterward.
Microsoft is up about 4% after hours on a beat. Azure grew 48% cc y/y in the quarter (vs 42% cc last quarter, and a 47% like-for-like bogey), and Q2 is guided to 49%-50% cc.

Both hyperscalers reporting (MSFT, GOOGL) had capex below expectations for the quarter while full-year guidance was reiterated. Microsoft's Q1 capex was lower because third-party capacity was delayed, which pushed neocloud suppliers lower after hours.
GS expects the ability to spend the capex, given power and grid constraints, to become a bigger gating factor for AI infrastructure.
Alphabet is down 7% after hours. Cloud growth was solid, but Search growth of +12% vs the +14% expected is in focus and is likely to feed a share-loss narrative.

ServiceNow is down 17% after hours. It showed AI attach, but growth is decelerating: the Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc missed Street (19%) and the buyside bar (~19.5-20%), and the EBIT margin guide was worse. The stock had risen 60%+ since Q2 earnings.

Dassault Systemes' Q3 beat is being questioned on quality (driven by licences, with the full-year upgrade largely reflecting the ArisGlobal acquisition). GS says the NOW and DSY prints make SAP look good relative.

Marvell is reported (Bloomberg, Reuters) to be in advanced talks to buy Lumentum (market cap about $83bn), with a deal possibly as soon as next week. Lumentum rose 9-11% after hours and Marvell fell more than 8% on financing and integration concerns around a stock-heavy deal.

Optical read-across is positive for the CPO supply chain. Coherent is a direct peer, and in Europe Nokia looks the clearest beneficiary, with positive implications for Aixtron. Nvidia has invested about $2bn in each of Marvell, Lumentum and Coherent.
Deutsche Telekom's plan to combine with T-Mobile US has hit a snag. DT chose not to submit a formal bid for now, partly because of works council pushback (Bloomberg, unconfirmed).
Reuters reports the DOJ is examining the competitive implications of Nvidia's proposed deal, alongside its broader probe into the company's acquisitions and business practices.
Samsung fell 4%: results were fine but investors were disappointed that buyback and dividend details come only in January, after SK Hynix announced a 100 trillion won total return package.

STMicro Q3 beat and guided Q4 above the Street (revenue $4.15bn, about 1% ahead; gross margin 39% vs Street 38.1%). Clean EBIT was $429mn, 14% ahead. Estimates should rise by mid-to-high single digits. Demand increased on strong bookings, and distributor inventory is below targets.

WPP Q3 organic net sales were -2.1% vs GSe/Vuma consensus of -3.3%/-3.2%. WPP Media returned to +0.3% growth, while WPP Creative declined 5.0%. The company retained its H2 outlook and FY26 EBIT margin guidance of 12-13%.
Indra missed in Q3 (revenue 3% and EBIT 7% below) but reiterated guidance (EBIT >700m, sales >7bn, FCF >375m vs 424.9m expected). GS sees the miss as phasing.
KLA beat and raised. It sees accelerating growth in 2H CY26 into 2027, raised 2026 WFE to about $155bn, and now expects 2027 WFE of $200bn (+30% y/y, from $190bn / 25%).

T-Mobile US posted small beats and strong postpaid adds, but only about half of the $220mn EBITDA beat (+$100mn) flowed through to the raised 2026E guidance. Device subsidy timing and lower prepaid and wholesale outlook weigh on Q4.

ASM International guided 2027 revenue to EUR 5.7bn (about 35% y/y), mirroring expected WFE growth with no cushion. Management expects 1.4nm to be a bigger contributor than 2nm in 2027, gross margin of 52% to hold, and strong China demand in mature foundry.

Adyen: the debate is whether higher investment lifts growth above roughly 20%. Dropping the FY28 margin target of at least 55% adds uncertainty. The stock is down 12%, which the author thinks is overdone, but a PM says it stays in the penalty box until communication improves. Next catalyst is the February 2027 outlook.
Renesas Q3 operating profit was JPY 150.5bn (34.6% margin), above estimates, with strong IIoT margins. Q4 sales guidance of JPY 454.0bn is in line.

KPN is confident of a Q4 broadband recovery after a 7k consumer base decline tied to a penalty-free exit window. Telenor's call suggested slower recoveries in Norway and Finland, with aggressive promotions continuing.

FCC approved Amazon Leo's $11.5bn acquisition of Globalstar, giving Amazon 25 MHz of mobile-satellite spectrum and about two dozen active satellites. Amazon committed to maintain Emergency SOS and Find My for Apple devices, which use about 85% of Globalstar capacity.

US trading flow: AI/semis showed some demand after 2-3 weeks of little buying, mainly from long-only accounts. Asset managers and hedge funds were small net buyers, with desk activity at 4 on a 1-10 scale.

FOMC held the funds rate at 3.75-4.00%. Governor Cook and President Hammack dissented, preferring a 25bp hike. The statement upgraded economic activity to 'strong' from 'solid' and said inflation remains elevated.
Derivatives desk: a quiet session with a low S&P implied move into the FOMC. S&P and NDX vols were offered across the curve and skew relaxed slightly as spot closed up small.

sector_views.rationale: NOW's decelerating cRPO guide and questions over DSY's beat quality raise the bar after the sector's recent run. SAP looks relatively strong.
KLA and ASM both point to accelerating 2027 WFE growth (about $200bn, +30%) with high visibility.
The Marvell/Lumentum talks signal scarcity of laser light sources for CPO, with positive read-across to Coherent, Nokia and Aixtron.

earnings_insights: MSFT FQ1 (reported 10/29): Azure +48% cc y/y vs 42% cc in FQ4, total revenue growth 19% (19% cc) and about 2% above the Street, Cloud gross margin 66% vs 65%. Commercial RPO $677bn vs $678bn last quarter. Capex $45.2bn including finance leases (+30% y/y vs Street +48%). FQ2 guide: Azure +49%-50% cc and capex above $50bn.
GOOGL (reported 10/29, after hours): Search growth +12% vs +14% expected; Cloud growth solid.

NOW Q3 (reported 10/29): subscription revenue +20.5% to $3.98bn, 50bps above guidance and in line with sellside but short of buyside ~$4.01-4.03B. cRPO +21% cc beat guide but was below the ~21.5-22% buyside bar. Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc vs Street 19% and bulls at ~19.5-20%. EBIT margin guide worse.
ORCL capital markets day (10/29): reaffirmed long-term targets of $225B+ revenue, 40%+ margins and $21+ EPS by FY30. Expects an additional 7GW of data center capacity in the next couple of years.
KLAC (reported 10/29): beat and raise. 2026 WFE guided to about $155bn (from low-$150bn) and 2027 WFE to $200bn (from $190bn).
TMUS Q3 (reported 10/29): EBITDA beat of $220mn, with $100mn flowing to the raised 2026E guidance. Postpaid adds were strong.

STMicro Q3 (reported 10/29): revenue 2% ahead and gross profit 2% ahead, gross margin 37.3%. Reported EBIT missed by 2%. Clean EBIT ex restructuring/impairment charges (EUR 55m) and phase-out costs (7m) was $429mn, 14% ahead. Q4 guide: revenue $4.15bn (1% above Street, +10.5% q/q +/-350bps) and gross margin 39% +/-200bps vs Street 38.1%.
WPP Q3 (reported 10/29): organic net sales -2.1% vs GSe/Vuma consensus of -3.3%/-3.2%. Net sales of GBP 2,411m, about 1% ahead. WPP Media +0.3% (vs -2.8% in Q2), WPP Creative -5.0% (vs -3.5% in Q2).
Indra Q3 (reported 10/29): revenue missed by 3% and EBIT by 7%. Guidance reiterated: EBIT >EUR 700m (vs 698.8m expected), sales >EUR 7bn (vs 6.9bn expected), FCF >EUR 375m (vs 424.9m expected).
ASM International (reported 10/29): 2027 revenue guide EUR 5.7bn, implying about 35% y/y growth. Gross margin currently 52%. Consensus models about 20% growth in 2028.
Renesas Q3 (reported 10/29): operating profit JPY 150.5bn and 34.6% operating margin, above estimates. Q4 sales guidance JPY 454.0bn in line.
Dassault Systemes Q3 (reported 10/28): beat driven by licences. Full-year upgrade largely reflects the ArisGlobal acquisition. Capital markets day is on the 17th.
Samsung Q3 (reported 10/29): results fine, stock -4% on buyback/dividend details being deferred to January.
KPN Q3: consumer broadband base fell 7k on churn in a penalty-free exit window. Management expects positive net adds in Q4.

tension_points.bull_case: NOW showed AI attach and cRPO of 21% cc beat guide, and SAP's beat looks strong relative to peers.
tension_points.bear_case: NOW's Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% cc missed Street (19%) and the buyside bar (~19.5-20%), and the EBIT margin guide was worse after a 60%+ run. DSY's beat quality is also questioned.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further cRPO guide-downs: the Q4 cRPO guide of 18.5% is an early indicator of FY27 revenue growth.

tension_points.bull_case: Azure accelerated to 48% cc, guided to 49%-50%, and Microsoft reiterated full-year capex with acceleration expected in the second half of its fiscal year.
tension_points.bear_case: Capex came in below expectations because of third-party capacity delays, and power and grid realities could become a bigger gating factor on spending.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Continued capex shortfalls from delayed third-party capacity, with Q2 capex guided above $50bn as the next check.

tension_points.bull_case: A record 2026 customer cohort, US hiring, equity-based pay and acquisitions could extend growth above roughly 20%.
tension_points.bear_case: The FY28 margin target of at least 55% was dropped without a new medium-term framework, and the previous hiring push hit margins while growth held rather than accelerated.
tension_points.what_invalidates: The February 2027 outlook for revenue guidance, EBITDA and CapEx tests whether spending delivers growth, leverage and cash returns.
